# adv-930 — adversarial verification of the #930 fix

> **Two rounds.** Round 1 (below) refuted the original fix. Round 2 (at the foot of this file)
> re-verifies the case-fold repair and is the current result: **NOT REFUTED**.

---

# ROUND 1 — the original fix

**Claim under test (verbatim):** *Archiving must never relocate a directory that is not a project folder.*

**Surface:** the `isReservedWorkflowDirName` guard at the top of `archiveProjectDir` in the four
`*claim.js` copies, its callers (`cmdFinalize`, `cmdRelease`, both abandon sweeps, `sink-merge`), and
every other site that renames / copies / deletes a directory under `kaola-workflow/`.

**Analytical result: REFUTED.**

**Verdict: fail. findings_blocking: 1.** Confidence: high — the refutation is driven end-to-end
through the shipped CLI, with a baseline positive control and a lowercase negative control.

Baseline `68cb48f4`. All work done on APFS clone-on-write mirrors of the working tree under the
session scratchpad (`m930` = candidate; `base930` = `m930` with the four `*claim.js` copies replaced
by their HEAD blobs, sha256-verified against `git show HEAD:<path>`). **No tracked file was modified
and `git checkout --` was never run.** The in-flight `*sink-merge.js` / `test-sink-merge.js` edits
(#931) were left alone; where the sink mattered I read `git show HEAD:` rather than the working copy.

## The refutation, ranked

### R1 — CONFIRMED, BLOCKING. The predicate is exact-match; the filesystem it protects is case-insensitive. `--project Archive` bypasses the guard entirely and reproduces the full #930 destruction at exit 0.

`isReservedWorkflowDirName` tests `name === 'archive'`. This repository's volume **and** `os.tmpdir()`
are both case-insensitive (measured: `touch AbC && test -e abc` → true on both; `test -e ./claude.md`
→ true at the repo root). So `kaola-workflow/Archive` **is** `kaola-workflow/archive` on disk, while
`'Archive' === 'archive'` is `false` in the guard.

**Failure scenario, driven.** Fixture: a git repo whose `kaola-workflow/archive/` band holds a prior
archived run (`issue-900/workflow-state.md`, `issue-900/mission-list.md`), a linked worktree on
`workflow/case2` carrying an implementation commit, a claim state file written under the name
`Archive`, and a consumer `.gitignore` containing `*.md`. Command:

```
node scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js finalize --project Archive --keep-worktree   # cwd = the worktree
```

Result on the **candidate** tree:

```
exit 0
{"status":"closed","archived":true,
 "dest":".../kaola-workflow/archive/Archive",
 "closure_receipt":{"archive":"closed", ...}}
[workflow/case2 a364c28] chore: archive Archive
```

and on disk:

```
kaola-workflow/archive/   BEFORE (main + worktree, identical):
    .cache/final-validation.md
    issue-900/mission-list.md          <- a previous run's record
    issue-900/workflow-state.md
    workflow-state.md
kaola-workflow/archive/   AFTER:  (does not exist, in EITHER checkout)
```

The whole archive band is `rm -rf`'d in both checkouts, including the `archive/Archive/` copy the run
had just written into it — so the `dest` the receipt names does not exist either. Exit 0,
`archived: true`, `closure_receipt.archive: "closed"`, a `chore: archive Archive` commit authored on
the branch the sink merges to main. That is the #930 failure verbatim, with a larger blast radius
than the filed case.

**Mechanism.** With the guard bypassed, `archiveProjectDir` runs with `src = <wt>/kaola-workflow/Archive`
(the worktree's whole archive band) and `dest = <main>/kaola-workflow/archive/Archive`. `copyDir`
succeeds, so `v.ok` is true. `mainLive = <main>/kaola-workflow/Archive` — again the whole band —
is `mainLiveDisposable`, and `verifyArchiveComplete(mainLive, dest)` reports the freshly-created
`Archive/**` entries as missing at `dest/Archive/**`. That is normally what stops it. But
`repoWideIgnoredNames` (`claim.js:2614-2615`) strips every entry whose **basename** the repo ignores,
and a band of `.md` files under a `*.md` rule empties `missingFromMain` completely. Both
`fs.rmSync(src)` and `fs.rmSync(mainLive)` at `claim.js:2638-2639` then execute.

**Three controls, all driven on the same fixture:**

| control | tree | `--project` | exit | archive band after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | **baseline (HEAD)** | `Archive` | 0 | **destroyed, both checkouts** |
| B | **candidate** | `archive` | **1**, `archive_reserved_directory` | **fully preserved** |
| C | baseline (HEAD) | `archive` | 0 | destroyed, both checkouts |

Control B is the proof the guard is genuinely load-bearing — it saves this exact fixture. Control A
is the proof the hole is **pre-existing**, not a regression this candidate introduced. The only thing
between control B and control A is the case of one letter.

**Guard bypass without the `.gitignore` condition, also driven.** On an ordinary fixture (no
`*.md` rule, band holding a `.patch` file), `--project Archive` and `--project ARCHIVE` still walk
straight past the guard. Linked lane: exit 1 `archive_incomplete`, having left **6 files of untracked
residue at `kaola-workflow/archive/Archive/`** — a partial self-copy of the archive band, including
the prior run and the salvage patch. In-place lane: exit 1 `archive_exception` (EINVAL from
`rename archive -> archive/Archive`). Same fixture with `--project archive`: `archive_reserved_directory`,
zero residue. So the guard bypass is unconditional; only whether it ends in *loss* or in *residue*
depends on the repo's ignore rules.

**Scope note.** `.roadmap` has no analogous bypass — `startsWith('.')` is case-free. The hole is the
`archive` arm alone, and it is the arm the enumeration wording (`active-folders.js:240`, both
barrier-reap keep passes) writes exact-match too; those read `entry.name` from `readdirSync`, which
returns the on-disk name, so they are asking a different question of a different input and are not
affected. `archiveProjectDir` is the one site that tests the **caller-supplied** name.

```
finding: id=R1 scope=in_scope action=fix status=open severity=high fix_role=tdd-guide rationale=exact-match `name === 'archive'` on a case-insensitive filesystem lets `--project Archive` bypass the guard and destroy both archive bands at exit 0 with archived:true
```

### R2 — CONFIRMED, low. The refusal's `detail` sentence is false at the surface it is emitted on.

The candidate emits `"nothing was moved, copied, stamped or deleted"`. That is accurate about
`archiveProjectDir` in isolation, but the string is only ever surfaced on a **finalize** (or discard)
envelope, and `cmdFinalize` has already written into the reserved directory twice before reaching
the archive call:

- Step 8a `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts` (`claim.js:4084` → `mergeCopyDir` at `:3437`) copies main's
  `kaola-workflow/.roadmap/` **down over the worktree's**;
- `persistValidationToSummary` / `persistChangedPathsToSummary` (`:4218-4219`) **create**
  `kaola-workflow/.roadmap/finalization-summary.md`.

Measured on the candidate, `.roadmap`, linked lane, all four editions:

```
worktree kaola-workflow/.roadmap/  ADDED:   finalization-summary.md
worktree kaola-workflow/.roadmap/.cache/final-validation.md  d7548b691726 -> c5a93e233cc8 (overwritten)
```

Both writes are pre-existing machinery; the **false sentence** is candidate-authored. This is the
project's own "report outcomes faithfully" class, and the fix is one clause ("the archive step moved,
copied, stamped and deleted nothing"), not a mechanism.

Note the same gap in the pinned result: neither the walkthrough scenario nor
`test-forge-archive-scoping.js` asserts the reserved directory is unchanged as a **set** — both only
assert the enumerated foreign files still exist and match — so the added `finalization-summary.md`
passes both suites unseen.

```
finding: id=R2 scope=in_scope action=fix status=open severity=low fix_role=implementer rationale=the refusal detail claims nothing was written while the same finalize transaction created finalization-summary.md inside the reserved directory and overwrote its .cache/final-validation.md
```

### R3 — CONFIRMED, informational, PRE-EXISTING and out of #930's declared scope. The claim-side rollback `rm -rf`s the reserved directory.

`claimProject` (`claim.js:1184-1192`) treats an existing `kaola-workflow/.roadmap` with no
`workflow-state.md` as "orphaned stateless dir — fall through and reclaim", and its transaction
rollback at `claim.js:1263` is `fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` over
`projectDir(root, project)`. A throw from `persistSelectionRecord` or `writeState` therefore deletes
the entire `kaola-workflow/.roadmap/` tree. Reachable, narrow, and unaffected by this fix — the owner
ruled the claim side out of scope and `active-folders.js:240` was correctly left alone. Recording it
because the brief asked for every mover under `kaola-workflow/`, not as a defect in the candidate.

```
finding: id=R3 scope=pre_existing action=none status=open severity=medium fix_role=none rationale=claimProject's rollback rm -rf's the adopted project dir, which for a reserved name is the reserved directory itself; pre-existing and outside the archive side this issue scoped
```

### R4 — the `exports` gap: **the team lead's reasoning HOLDS.** Not refuted.

Driven, candidate and baseline, both lanes:

- `archive/exports/` **already exists** (a salvage patch present): `archiveProjectDir` collision-suffixes
  (`claim.js:2552` / `:2648`, both lanes) and the run lands on
  `kaola-workflow/archive/exports.archived-<ts>/`. `LOST from main archive band: []` — the salvage
  patch `exports/issue-42-2026-01-01.patch` survives byte-for-byte. Candidate and baseline identical.
  **Nothing is destroyed.** The reasoning is correct.
- `archive/exports/` **does not exist**: `dest` is exactly `kaola-workflow/archive/exports`
  (driven: `exit=0 archived=true dest=kaola-workflow/archive/exports`). Still no loss, but two
  non-destructive consequences worth recording, neither of which changes the ruling:
  1. every later `exportWorktreeDiff` (`claim.js:334`) writes salvage patches **into the archived run
     folder**;
  2. `projectRelativeArtifactPath` returns `null` for everything under `archive/exports/`
     (`adaptive-schema.js:844`), so that archived run's kernel artifacts become invisible to the
     classifier.

Also confirmed: `kaola-workflow/exports/` has never existed, and `exports` has never been a
`workflow_project` value or an archive directory name (see R5's audit).

### R5 — the `archive` control's prior behaviour is characterised wrongly in the impl report and in the walkthrough comment.

The impl report states the `archive` control's before-state was *"`EINVAL` … (main lane) /
`archive_incomplete` naming 8384 entries (worktree lane), both exit 1"*, and the new walkthrough
scenario calls `archive` *"the one reserved name that already survives today (its rename dead-ends
EINVAL)"*. **Control C above refutes both for the worktree lane**: at HEAD, `--project archive` on a
linked run exits **0** and destroys the whole band in both checkouts. The fix handles this correctly
(control B), so nothing is wrong with the *change* — but "nothing is lost either way", which the
report gives as the reason the control could change mechanism freely, is not true of the lane the
real workflow uses. Prose only; no code consequence.

### Finding the next bypass — exhaustively, against the filesystem rather than against `toLowerCase`

The right question is not "does `toLowerCase` agree with APFS" but "**which strings does this
filesystem resolve to the reserved directory, and does the predicate refuse every one of them**". So
I created `kaola-workflow/archive` and `kaola-workflow/.roadmap`, recorded their inodes, and `stat`ed
candidate names — a lookup answers the aliasing question with no creation needed. The predicate under
test is extracted from the **shipped** `claim.js` text at run time, not re-typed.

**Sweep 1 — every BMP code point at every position of both base names, plus all four normalisation
forms: 952,275 probes.**
**Sweep 2 — every astral code point (U+10000–U+10FFFF) at every position: 15,728,640 probes.**

```
names the FILESYSTEM resolves to the target:  14   (BMP)   +   0   (astral)
  archive : Archive aRchive arChive arcHive archIve archiVe archivE
  .roadmap: .Roadmap .rOadmap .roAdmap .roaDmap .roadMap .roadmAp .roadmaP
  all refused by the shipped predicate: true / true
OPEN BYPASSES: 0
```

**16,680,915 probes, zero open bypasses.** Every single-code-point substitution in all of Unicode, at
every position of both reserved names, plus NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD of each — the only aliases this volume
produces are the 14 pure ASCII case flips, and the predicate refuses all 14.

Your named suspects were all measured, and every one is a **genuinely distinct directory** on this
volume, so *not* refusing them is correct rather than a hole: Turkish dotless `ı` (`archıve`), `İ`
(`ARCHİVE`), Kelvin sign, fullwidth (`ａrchive`, `ＡＲＣＨＩＶＥ`), Cyrillic-`е` homoglyph,
superscript `ⁱ`, ZWSP/NBSP/soft-hyphen/ZWJ/ZWNJ/BOM at every position, combining marks at every
position, `archivé` in both NFC and NFD, and the length-changing fold `archi` + U+0307 + `ve`.
`fs.statSync` on each returns `ENOENT` or a different inode.

**A 147-case multi-character and path-form sweep** found exactly four strings the filesystem aliases
to `archive`: `archive/`, `./archive`, `archive/.`, `archive//`. **All four are rejected by
`isSafeName`**, whose `assert` at `claim.js:2449` runs *before* the guard — so they never reach the
mover; they surface as a thrown assert caught by `archiveProjectDirSafely` into `archive_exception`.
Your attack 2 is answered: `archive.`, ` archive`, `archive ` (trailing space), `archive\t` and the
NBSP/ZWSP forms are all distinct directories on APFS — macOS does **not** strip trailing dots or
spaces the way NTFS does, so there is nothing to close there.

**Scope of the bound, stated honestly.** This proves the predicate covers every *single-code-point*
alias plus the normalisation forms plus the tested multi-character set, **on this volume**. It is not
a proof about every filesystem: a case-insensitive volume with a different fold table (an older HFS+
volume, a case-insensitive ZFS dataset, NTFS over a share) could in principle alias a pair this sweep
did not produce. Nothing in the tree detects that. This is the strongest bound I can measure rather
than assert.

## 2. The over-refusal trade — measured, and it does not bite

Newly refused set = `{n : n.toLowerCase() === 'archive'} \ {'archive'}` = 127 ASCII case variants.
Audited against the **new** predicate:

- **41** distinct `workflow_project:` values in the whole of git history — none matches `/^archive$/i`.
- **400** distinct archive directory names ever committed — none matches `/^archive$/i`.
- **170** distinct live project directory names ever committed under `kaola-workflow/` — the only
  `/^archive$/i` match is the literal lowercase band itself, which is not a project.
- The only dot-prefixed live names that have **ever** existed are `.origin` and `.roadmap`, both
  genuinely reserved.
- No fixture, helper or production script passes a case variant of `archive` as a project name; every
  direct `archiveProjectDir` call outside the four `claim.js` copies still passes an ordinary name.

The one over-refusal the probe surfaced is `.roadmap ` (trailing space) — a distinct directory that

## 3. R2 — the repair is correct on the surface it is emitted on

New detail: `"kaola-workflow/<name> is a reserved directory, not a project folder; the archive step
moved, copied, stamped and deleted nothing"`. Driven, all four editions: main's `.roadmap`
byte-identical, no archive destination created, no rename, no stamp. **True as scoped, and it no
longer speaks for the transaction.** The added comment paragraph explaining why is accurate,
including its claim that the sink and the abandon sweeps reach the function without either write.

The test surface closed the matching gap: `test-forge-archive-scoping.js` now asserts the reserved
directory's file **SET**, tolerating exactly one named addition
(`KNOWN_ADDITIONS = new Set(['finalization-summary.md'])`), so the next unplanned addition cannot
arrive unseen. It probes case-sensitivity at run time and skips the alias arm where there is no
subject; on this box the arm **ran** — `930[claude/canonical/Archive]`, `930[codex/Archive]`,
`930[gitlab/Archive]`, `930[gitea/Archive]` all present in the output, not skipped.

### On `tests-930`'s correction about `.cache/final-validation.md` — I do not accept it

You asked for my read rather than an adjudication, so: **their measurement is right and their
inference is wrong.** A fixture whose two roots hold *identical digests* cannot observe an overwrite
— copying a file over a byte-identical copy leaves no trace. That control is vacuous for this
question; it is not evidence the overwrite does not happen.

The overwrite is the shipped rule, readable without any fixture:
`mergeCopyDir(srcDir, destDir, FINALIZE_MIRROR_DEST_OWNED, FINALIZE_MIRROR_TREE_BOUND)` at
`claim.js:3462`, where `FINALIZE_MIRROR_DEST_OWNED = {'workflow-state.md', 'workflow-tasks.json'}`
(`:3310`) and `FINALIZE_MIRROR_TREE_BOUND = {'.cache/chain-receipt.json', '.cache/<outcome log>'}`
(`:3324`). `.cache/final-validation.md` is in **neither** keep-set, so main's copy overwrites the
worktree's unconditionally whenever both exist. And the two copies do differ in a real linked run:
the file carries `validated_candidate_hash` from `computeCodeTreeHash` over the tree the recorder's
shell was in, and finalize's own operator hint says so in as many words — *"the gate hashes the tree
its own shell is in, and a linked worktree and main differ until the branch merges"*. Re-measured
this round on the repaired tree, all four editions:
`wt .cache/final-validation.md  d7548b691726 -> c5a93e233cc8` (main held `c5a93e233cc8`).

None of this changes the verdict. It is pre-existing machinery, unrelated to #930, and the reworded
detail no longer claims otherwise — so there is nothing here for this bundle to fix. I record it only
because the correction, left standing, would retire a true fact on the strength of a control that
could not have detected it.

## 5. Two documentation defects — recorded; neither is a counterexample to the claim

### R6 — all three shipped doc surfaces describe the OLD predicate. A reader learns that `Archive` is archivable.

The case-fold is the entire substance of this repair, and none of the three prose surfaces mentions
it. Measured: `grep -ci "case-insensit|case-fold|toLowerCase|case variant"` → **0** in `docs/api.md`,
**0** in `docs/workflow-state-contract.md`; the 5 hits in `CHANGELOG.md` are all pre-existing entries
about unrelated case-folding work.

- `docs/api.md:815` — *"a reserved directory under `kaola-workflow/` — `archive`, or any name
  beginning with `.`"*
- `docs/workflow-state-contract.md:145` — *"refuses `archive` and every dot-prefixed name outright"*
- `CHANGELOG.md:17` — *"for `archive` and every dot-prefixed name"*

Each is a complete-sounding enumeration that omits 127 of the names the shipped predicate refuses.
The `api.md` row's recovery advice compounds it — *"release or discard it and re-claim under a real
project name"* — because a reader whose run is named `Archive` has no way to learn from that page why
it was refused. CLAUDE.md requires these surfaces be updated on a user-visible change; they were
updated, to describe the predicate as it stood one revision ago.

Secondary, same row: `api.md:815` closes with *"so nothing was moved, copied, stamped or deleted **in
any checkout**"* — the sentence deliberately rescoped in the code's own `detail` this round,
reinstated in prose and widened. It is defensible where it sits (that table is the **sink's**
`sink_incomplete` step list, and the sink's finalize step calls `archiveProjectDir` with no Step-8a
mirror and no `persistValidationToSummary`), but the sink's earlier `merge` step does
`sinkLandStagedUnion(wtStageDir, mainProjDir)` into `kaola-workflow/<project>/`, so "in any checkout"
is broader than the guard can support. Worth a second look given the code text was just narrowed for
exactly this reason.
